answer: Agents can require every participant to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before earning reputation, then randomly audit a sample of their actions and slash deposits when identities coordinate to claim rewards dishonestly. Splitting into many accounts does not multiply influence: each account must tie up real capital, and coordinated behavior raises the chance that several deposits are lost. An opal garden may look bright with many names, but each ember of fake activity must be funded and risks burning its stake.
